text.p: Typhoon Sally continues to track near the coast of Guangxi China and north Vietnam. Shipping in the far north Gulf of Tonkin is still at risk since part of the circulation is still over water and seas are likely rough. Sally should track inland in northern Vietnam during the next 12-24 hours. Conditions improve in the north Gulf of Tonkin. Heavy rains inland in northern Vietnam should cause flooding and strong winds. Damage to property appears likely.

Hurricane Hortense, with 80 mph winds, is about 100 miles south of St. Croix in the eastern Caribbean. Shipping in the region will be at risk for at least the next 24-48 hours. Hortense is expected to track west-northwest this period and move into Hispanola within 36 hours. Flooding rains and strong winds would cause damage through the island during this time, especially along the south coast. However, Hortense has been drifting towards the northwest during the past few hours. If this motion continues it would become a risk to Puerto Rico in a fairly short period of time.
Tropical cyclone 03s become a decreasing risk to shipping as it dissipates in the south Indian Ocean.
Tropical depression 24w may threaten Luzon Philippines this period as a weak tropical storm.
